messages.content: How much electricity will I need for my 2000 sq ft home?

function.name: solar_panel_calculate_need
function.description: Calculate the number of solar panels needed for a house based on the square footage and average sunlight hours. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

square_footage.description: The square footage of the house. This is a float type value.

average_sunlight_hours.description: The average hours of sunlight received. This is a float type value.

usage_efficiency.description: The efficiency of energy usage in the home, default is 0.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
A 2 000‑sq‑ft house typically uses somewhere between **25–45 kWh per day** (≈ 750–1 350 kWh per month), depending on:

| Factor | Typical impact |
|--------|----------------|
| Climate & heating/cooling load | Higher in extreme climates |
| Insulation & windows | Better insulation → lower usage |
| Appliances & electronics | More/older appliances increase load |
| Occupancy patterns | More occupants or high‑energy devices raise usage |

So, as a ballpark, expect **about 30 kWh/day** (≈ 900 kWh/month) for a reasonably insulated, moderately occupied 2 000‑sq‑ft home in a temperate region. If you’re in a very hot or cold area, or have many electric appliances (EV charger, heat pump, etc.), you may be closer to the upper end of that range.
